text:
In a plane electromagnetic wave, the directions
of electric field and magnetic field are
represented by $\widehat{k}$ and $2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}$, respectively.
What is the unit vector along direction of
propagation of the wave?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{E}\times \vec{B}=\widehat{k}\times \left (2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}\right )$

= $2\widehat{k}\times \hat{i}-2\widehat{k}\times \hat{j}$

= $\left (2\hat{j}+2\hat{i}\right )$

Unit vector along $\vec{E}\times \vec{B}$ = $\frac{\left (2\hat{j}+2\hat{i}\right )}{2\sqrt{2}}$

= $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left (\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
In a Young’s double slit experiment, 16 fringes
are observed in a certain segment of the
screen when light of a wavelength 700 nm is
used. If the wavelength of light is changed to
400 nm, the number of fringes observed in the
same segment of the screen would be
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the length of segment is "$l$"

Let N is the no. of fringes in "$l$"
and w is fringe width.

$\therefore$ Nw = $l$

$\Rightarrow$ N$\left (\frac{λD}{d}\right )$ = $l$

As in both cases segment length is same.

$\therefore$ $\frac{N_{1}λ_{1}D}{d}=l$

 and $\frac{N_{2}λ_{2}D}{d}=l$

$\therefore$ $\frac{N_{1}λ_{1}D}{d}$ = $\frac{N_{2}λ_{2}D}{d}$

$\Rightarrow$ $N_{1}λ_{1}$ = $N_{2}λ_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $16 × 700 = N_{2} × 400$

$\Rightarrow$ $N_{2} = 28$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
When the temperature of a metal wire is
increased from $0^{o}C$ to $10^{o}C$, its length
increases by 0.02%. The percentage change in
its mass density will be closest to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\frac{\Delta L}{L}$ = 0.02%

We know, $\Delta$L = L$α\Delta$T

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta L}{L}=α\Delta T$ = 0.02

Also, $β$ = 2$α$

$\Rightarrow$ $β\Delta T=2α\Delta T$ = 0.04

Density($ρ$) = $\frac{M}{AL}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta ρ}{ρ}=\frac{\Delta M}{M}-\frac{\Delta A}{A}-\frac{\Delta L}{L}$ ( $\frac{\Delta M}{M}$ = 0 as M = constant)

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta ρ}{ρ}=\frac{\Delta A}{A}+\frac{\Delta L}{L}$

= $β\Delta T+α\Delta T$

= 0.04 + 0.02 = 0.06 %

text:
An ideal gas in a closed container is slowly
heated. As its temperature increases, which of
the following statements are true?

(A) the mean free path of the molecules
decreases.

(B) the mean collision time between the
molecules decreases.

(C) the mean free path remains unchanged.

(D) the mean collision time remains unchanged.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mean free path of molecules of an ideal gas is given as:

$λ$ = $\frac{V}{\sqrt{2}πd^{2}N}$

where : V = Volume of container

N = No of molecules

Mean free path is independent of temperature hence with increasing temp since volume of container does not change (closed container), so mean free path
is unchanged.

Average collision time = 
     $λ$
     $V_{av}$

and $V_{av}$ $\propto$ $\sqrt{T}$

$\therefore$ Average collision time $\propto$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}$

Hence with increase in temperature the average collision time decreases.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
In a hydrogen atom the electron makes a
transition from $(n + 1)^{th}$ level to the $n^{th}$ level.
If n >> 1, the frequency of radiation emitted is
proportional to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The energy of the $n$th level of hydrogen is $E_{n}=-\dfrac{E_{0}}{n^{2}}$, where $E_{0}=13.6\text{eV}$.

For the transition from level $(n+1)$ to level $n$, the emitted photon carries the energy difference:

$hν=E_{n+1}-E_{n}=E_{0}\left (\dfrac{1}{n^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{(n+1)^{2}}\right )=E_{0}\dfrac{2n+1}{n^{2}(n+1)^{2}}$

For $n\gg 1$, $2n+1\approx 2n$ and $(n+1)^{2}\approx n^{2}$, so

$hν\approx E_{0}\dfrac{2n}{n^{4}}=\dfrac{2E_{0}}{n^{3}}\Rightarrow ν\propto \dfrac{1}{n^{3}}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

solution.body:

 (B) at t = T,

 displacement (x) = A $\Rightarrow$ x maximum,

at t = $\frac{T}{4}$, x = 0

When an AC signal of frequency 1000 Hz is

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

= 1.1 $\times$ $10^{–2} H$

text:
Two uniform circular discs are rotating
independently in the same direction around
their common axis passing through their
centres. The moment of inertia and angular
velocity of the first disc are $0.1 kg-m^{2}$ and 10
rad $s^{–1}$ respectively while those for the second
one are $0.2 kg-m^{2}$ and 5 rad $s^{–1}$ respectively. At
some instant they get stuck together and start
rotating as a single system about their common
axis with some angular speed. The kinetic
energy of the combined system is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Angular momentum conserved for the system

$I_{1}ω_{1}$ $+ I_{2}ω_{2}$ $= (I_{1} + I_{2})ω_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ 0.1 × 10 + 0.2 × 5 = (0.1 + 0.2) × $ω_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω_{f}$ = $\frac{20}{3}$

Kinetic energy of combined disc system

= $\frac{1}{2}(I_{1}+I_{2})ω_{f}^{2}$

= $\frac{1}{2}(0.1+0.2)\left (\frac{20}{3}\right )^{2}$

= $\frac{20}{3}J$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
A charge Q is distributed over two concentric
conducting thin spherical shells radii r and
R (R > r). If the surface charge densities on the
two shells are equal, the electric potential at
the common centre is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the charges on inner and outer spheres are $Q_{1}$ and $Q_{2}$.

$\therefore$ $Q_{1} + Q_{2} = Q  ...(1)$

Since charge density '$σ$' is same for both spheres, so

$σ$ = $\frac{Q_{1}}{4πr^{2}}=\frac{Q_{2}}{4πR^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{Q_{1}}{Q_{2}}=\frac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}$ ....(2)

From (1) and (2),

$\frac{Q_{2}r^{2}}{R^{2}}+Q_{2}=Q$

$\Rightarrow$ $Q_{2} =$ $\frac{QR^{2}}{(r^{2}+R^{2})}$

$\therefore$ $Q_{1} =$ $\frac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}.\frac{QR^{2}}{(r^{2}+R^{2})}$ = $\frac{Qr^{2}}{(r^{2}+R^{2})}$

Potential at centre 'O' = $\frac{kQ_{1}}{r}+\frac{kQ_{2}}{R}$

= $k\left [\frac{Qr^{2}}{r(r^{2}+R^{2})}+\frac{QR^{2}}{R(r^{2}+R^{2})}\right ]$

= $\frac{kQ(r+R)}{(r^{2}+R^{2})}$

= $\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}\frac{(R+r)}{(R^{2}+r^{2})}$Q
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
A capillary tube made of glass of radius 0.15
mm is dipped vertically in a beaker filled with
methylene iodide (surface tension $= 0.05 Nm^{–1}$,
density $= 667 kg m^{–3})$ which rises to height h in
the tube. It is observed that the two tangents
drawn from liquid-glass interfaces (from opp.
sides of the capillary) make an angle of $60^{o}$
with one another. Then h is close to $(g = 10 ms^{–2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At each wall the liquid surface meets the glass at the angle of contact $θ$, so the tangent drawn there makes angle $θ$ with the vertical wall. The tangents from opposite sides are symmetric about the axis of the tube, so the angle between them is $2θ$:


[IMG]

$2θ=60^{\circ }\Rightarrow θ=30^{\circ }$

With $r=0.15\text{mm}=1.5\times 10^{-4}\text{m}$, the capillary rise is

$h=\dfrac{2T\cos θ}{ρgr}=\dfrac{2\times 0.05\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{667\times 10\times 1.5\times 10^{-4}}=\dfrac{0.0866}{1.0005}\approx 0.087\text{m}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
A particle of mass m is moving along the x-axis
with initial velocity $u\hat{i}$. It collides elastically
with a particle of mass 10 m at rest and then
moves with half its initial kinetic energy (see
figure). If $\sin θ_{1}=\sqrt{n}\sin θ_{2}$ then value of n is
$________$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\frac{1}{2}mv_{1}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{1}^{2}=\frac{u^{2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{1}=\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}$  ......(1)

Also collision is elastic : $k_{i}$
 $= k_{f}$

$\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}=\frac{1}{2}mv_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}(10m)v_{2}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{1}{2}mu^{2}=\frac{1}{2}(10m)v_{2}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2}^{2}=\frac{u^{2}}{20}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2}=\frac{u}{\sqrt{20}}$

By momentum conservation along y :

$m_{1}v_{1}\sin $ $θ_{1}$ $= m_{2}v_{2}\sin $ $θ_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $mv_{1}\sin $ $θ_{1}$ $= 10mv_{2}\sin $ $θ_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}$sin $θ_{1}$ = 10 $\times$ $\frac{u}{\sqrt{20}}$sin $θ_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ sin $θ_{1}$ = $\sqrt{10}$ sin $θ_{2}$

$\therefore$ n = 10

 So no current is there in branch ADB

$\therefore$ Effective circuit of current flow :

$R_{eq} =$ $\left (\frac{4\times 2}{4+2}\right )+2$

$R_{eq} =$ $\frac{4}{3}+2$ = $\frac{10}{3}\Omega$

i = $\frac{10}{\frac{10}{3}}$ = 3A

So potential difference across AEB

= 2 × 1 + 2 × 3 = 8V

text:
A light ray enters a solid glass sphere of
refractive index $μ$ = $\sqrt{3}$ at an angle of incidence
$60^{o}$. The ray is both reflected and refracted at
the farther surface of the sphere. The angle (in
degrees) between the reflected and refracted
rays at this surface is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


By Snell's law at $S_{1}$ :

1 $\times$ sin 60° = $\sqrt{3}$ sin r

$\Rightarrow$ $r = 30^{o}$

As $S_{2}$ :

$\sqrt{3}\sin r=1\sin e$

$\Rightarrow$ $e = 60^{o}$

Now, r
 + $θ$ $+ e = 180^{o}$
